Q: Check if index a primary key in MySQL A:

Instead of I_S.statistics, check I_S.table_constraints. The latter view has a column constraint_type which tells you which constraint is the primary key of the table.

mysql> create table test.t (id int primary key);

mysql> select * from information_schema.table_constraints where table_schema='test'\G
*************************** 1. row ***************************
CONSTRAINT_CATALOG: def
 CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA: test
   CONSTRAINT_NAME: PRIMARY
      TABLE_SCHEMA: test
        TABLE_NAME: t
   CONSTRAINT_TYPE: PRIMARY KEY
          ENFORCED: YES

Q: Auto delete functionality in inventory table => when the quantity for the item reaches 0 A:

You are getting this error because MySQL does not allow a trigger to modify the same table that fired it, when using an AFTER UPDATE trigger.

In your case:

AFTER UPDATE ON inventory

and inside the trigger you are doing:

DELETE FROM inventory

This causes MySQL to block the operation with:

Can't update table 'inventory' in stored function/trigger because it is already used by the statement which invoked this trigger

✔ Correct Approach

If you really want to handle this inside the database, use a BEFORE UPDATE trigger instead.

DELIMITER //

CREATE TRIGGER before_update_inventory
BEFORE UPDATE ON inventory
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    -- Update user space
    UPDATE user
    SET inventory_space = inventory_space + (OLD.quantity - NEW.quantity)
    WHERE user_id = NEW.user_id;

    -- If quantity becomes zero or negative, remove row
    IF NEW.quantity <= 0 THEN
        DELETE FROM inventory
        WHERE inventory_id = OLD.inventory_id;
    END IF;
END//

DELIMITER ;

Since this runs before the row update is finalized, MySQL allows it.

🚀 Even Better Design (Recommended)

From a database design perspective, this logic is cleaner and safer if handled in the application layer.

Instead of updating quantity to 0 and relying on a trigger:

DELETE FROM inventory
WHERE inventory_id = ? AND quantity <= 0;

Triggers that modify the same table often create maintenance and debugging complexity.

Summary

  • AFTER UPDATE cannot modify the same table

  • Use BEFORE UPDATE if you must use a trigger

  • Prefer handling delete logic in application code

Q: How can I select a single field for all documents in a MongoDB collection? A:

For a single update:

db.collection_name.update({ field_name_1: ("value")}, { $set: { field_name_2 : "new_value"  }});

For MultiUpdate:

db.collection_name.updateMany({ field_name_1: ("value")}, { $set: {field_name_2 : "new_value" }});

Make sure the indexes are proper.
